data.title: Bitcoin ETF outflows hit $635M as BTC price tests $81K support
data.description:
Spot Bitcoin [BTC] ETF recorded its biggest outflows since June 2025 on the 22nd of October, 2026, worth $635.5 million.

On the same day, BlackRock’s IBIT led the withdrawals with $254.1 million. This was followed by Fidelity’s FBTC at $217.5 million, ARK 21Shares’ ARKB at $109.4 million, Bitwise’s BITB at $27.4 million, and Grayscale’s GBTC at $29.5 million.

In fact, together, these products accounted for the bulk of the daily outflow. Meanwhile, on the other hand, Morgan Stanley’s MSBT recorded a relatively small $2.3 million inflow that provided little offset to the broader selling pressure.

Trend reversal

The scale of the withdrawals was particularly striking because it erased the positive momentum built up during the preceding two sessions, which had collectively attracted more than $1.05 billion.

In fact, according to AMBCrypto’s recent report, Bitcoin ETFs recorded a massive $663 million in inflows, marking their largest single-day intake in two months.

At the same time, Switzerland’s FINMA approved a physically backed Bitcoin fund, BBIT, for retail investors, with trading expected to begin on the SIX Swiss Exchange in November.

Bitcoin is back near the $81K radar

This BTC ETF rollercoaster came as Bitcoin was trading at $81,612.79 at press time after a modest drop in the past 24 hours but a drop of over 5% in the past month.

In other words, Bitcoin is once again back in the playground, where it is testing the $81,000 level. That said, Glassnode describes this price level as the estimated cost basis of investors in U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs.

For those unaware, the ETF cost basis refers to the average price at which investors acquired Bitcoin exposure through these funds. This level usually influences investor behavior.

So, if BTC remains above $81,000, the level could act as support and help stabilize the market. However, a sustained break below the $81K price level could weaken sentiment, particularly among investors who entered the market around this price.

Did altcoin ETFs mirror BTC ETFs?

On the other hand, other altcoin ETFs somewhat followed a similar pattern as BTC ETFs.

According to SoSo Value data, Ethereum [ETH] ETFs recorded $110.50 million in outflows, followed by Solana [SOL] ETF, which saw $8.51 million in outflows, and Hyperliquid [HYPE] ETF, which saw $7.88 million worth of outflows.

Notably, the newly launched Zcash [ZEC] ETF recorded $14.23 million in inflows, followed by the XRP ETF, which saw inflows worth $3.55 million all this on the 22nd of October.

Final Summary

  • BlackRock’s IBIT, Fidelity’s FBTC, ARK 21Shares’ ARKB, Bitwise’s BITB, and Grayscale’s GBTC accounted for the bulk of the daily outflow.
  • Bitcoin was trading at $81,612.79 at press time after a modest drop in the past 24 hours.

data.title: MemeCore – How falling trading volume could derail M’s 11% rally
data.description:
MemeCore [M] has recorded an 11% price surge over the last 24 hours at press time, after a sharp rejection from the 20-day EMA at $1.13. Despite the surge, the token lacks volume, with its trading volume shrinking by 4% over the same period.

However, MemeCore derivatives are leaning to the bulls. The token’s Open Interest (OI) has gained by 28% to $6.8 million over the last 24 hours, and long positions account for 54% of the total leveraged position.

Could the positive derivatives keep the current momentum going? 

Rising OI supports bullish positioning

On the derivatives, most on-chain metrics are leaning to the bulls. MemeCore‘s OI has recorded a 33% increase to 34 million over the last 24 hours. The spike indicates that traders are opening or maintaining more outstanding derivatives positions. 

Moreover, the rise suggests growing interest in the token as its price rebounds.

At the same time, it’s key for investors and traders in running positions to note that long positions account for more than 54% of leveraged positions, giving bullish traders a modest majority. 

This positioning could support further gains if buyers continue entering the market and the price maintains its upward trajectory.

Falling volume raises questions

According to the recent data, MemeCore’s trading volume has slipped by 4% to $3.79 million over the last 24 hours despite the overall weekly volume surging significantly.

On the short term, the daily drop creates a divergence between MemeCore’s price action and market participation. While the token price has gained 11%, lower turnover suggests that fewer tokens are changing hands than during the previous 24-hour period.

If volume continues to weaken, the rally could struggle to attract enough demand to extend its gains out of the current ranging structure. The increase in OI may reflect growing speculative exposure rather than sustained spot accumulation.

Besides, this combination also raises liquidation risks. If the price reverses, leveraged longs could face forced closures, adding to selling pressure.

Can MemeCore extend its rally?

MemeCore’s short-term outlook depends on whether derivatives demand translates into sustained buying. A continued growth in OI, a stable long bias, and recovering spot volume would strengthen the case for further bullish push.

On the daily chart, the 11% rally shows renewed price strength and has pushed the token past the 20-day Exponential Moving Average, but declining volume limits confirmation.

Final Summary

  • MemeCore has gained by more than 10% after a sharp rejection around the 20-day EMA at $1.13, while trading volume slips 4%.
  • The network’s Open Interest climbs to $7.3 million, with longs accounting for 54% of leveraged positions.

data.title: IRYS crypto jumps nearly 580% as traders betting against it lose $21M
data.description:
Irys [IRYS] surged nearly 580% over 24 hours on October 23, reaching around $0.144. A look at its daily chart showed that it recorded a session high near the $0.157 price area before it eased toward $0.142.

The rally coincided with heavy losses for traders betting on a price decline. Data showed that there were around $21.4 million in short liquidations, but the available data does not show what started the surge or how much forced buying contributed.

The rally accelerated well beyond four cents

IRYS began its daily session at around $0.0206. At the time of this writing, it was trading at almost 7x that level.

A look at the chart shows how the move developed. An initially gradual rise gathered pace after it passed the $0.04 price level, and a more positive move followed, taking the price toward $0.13.

It saw a brief pullback that interrupted that climb before buyers were then able to push the price higher again.

At the time of this writing, the daily chart showed a gain of roughly 592% with trading still ongoing.

Bets against IRYS took most of the liquidation losses

CoinMarketCap data showed around $24.2 million in total liquidations over 24 hours. Around $21.4 million came from shorts, compared with roughly $2.8 million from positions betting on higher prices.

Liquidations happen when an exchange forcibly closes a leveraged trade because the trader can no longer cover its losses.

Closing a short can involve buying back the asset or contract, potentially adding to upward pressure. But these totals cannot show how much of IRYS’s rally came from that process.

The data showed that outstanding futures positions also reached about $1.22 billion. That figure does not only mean that fresh cash is entering; the sharp price it saw raises the value.

What can the chart tell us now?

The session high near $0.157 provides an immediate reference for another advance. Below the latest price, the intraday pause around the $0.115–$0.13 price area offers an area to watch if selling returns, and sellers decide they want to take gains.

But that pause seen on the chart is too recent to call dependable support. But if it holds there through repeated pullbacks, it would mean that buyers are accepting the higher prices.

What is being seen is an interesting repricing and active trading, but where IRYS will settle once the initial surge slows remains to be seen.

Final Summary

  • IRYS gained nearly 580% over 24 hours, moving far beyond the brief’s earlier $0.04 level.
  • Short liquidations reached around $21.4 million, but the rally’s initial trigger is not known yet.

data.title: Zcash falls 7.34% as its rebound stalls—Can $1,200 hold?
data.description:
Zcash [ZEC] lost 7.34% on October 22, interrupting a recovery that saw it briefly go above the $1,300 price area. At the time of this writing, it was near the $1,225 price level, slightly above the day’s opening level.

The setback puts the $1,200 price area back in focus as futures numbers also decline. All this is coming as developers release software for the planned network upgrade in November, giving holders another development to watch apart from the daily swings.

A setback after a sharp recovery

ZEC had climbed from about $1,100 toward $1,350 before Thursday’s decline of over 7% erased most of that gain.

But despite the loss, the daily chart shows some ground remains below the price. ZEC held above its 50-day price average near the $1,193 price level, while its longer-term averages was considerably lower.

That leaves $1,190–$1,200 as the immediate test for it. If it holds this area, part of the recovery will be preserved. But if it continues to trade below it, it could go down to its recent lows around the $1,100 price area.

Buyers also face a nearby obstacle. Friday’s rise reached around $1,259 before easing, making the $1,240–$1,260 price area the first area to recover and hold. Beyond that, the latest rebound’s peak around the $1,320–$1,360 price area remains a harder challenge.

Futures exposure retreats alongside the price

CoinGlass’s open interest chart shows the dollar value of outstanding ZEC futures contracts falling after a recent jump toward $3 billion.

Its decline can show positions closing, but falling ZEC prices also reduce their dollar value.

November’s upgrade moves a step closer

The Zcash Foundation released Zebra 7.0.0 on October 22, providing stable software support for the forthcoming NU7 upgrade.

Activation is set for block 3,543,405, which is expected to be around November 5. The upgrade targets a reduction in block times from 75 seconds to 25 seconds, which will shorten the expected wait for a first transaction confirmation.

Daily ZEC issuance and the 21 million supply cap remain unchanged.

Final Summary

  • Zcash steadied near $1,225 after Thursday’s 7.34% loss, leaving $1,200 as an immediate test.
  • NU7 software is available ahead of expected November activation, while futures exposure has contracted.

data.title: XLM price edges higher, but Stellar’s October slide is proving hard to reverse
data.description:
Stellar [XLM] recovered slightly on October 23 after it saw a 4.57% decline the previous day. It was near $0.177 at the time of this writing, having briefly reached $0.179 earlier in the session.

The bounce has helped with its recovery, but it has only recovered a small part of what it lost. With it still below the levels it reached during its latest recovery attempt, buyers have more work to do before October’s negative trend can begin to change direction.

A promising rebound has already faded once

Earlier this week, XLM climbed from around $0.175 toward $0.187. That recovery gave traders some breathing room after several weeks of losses it saw.

But by October 22, the price had fallen back toward the $0.175 price area, taking away much of the advance. The small improvement it saw on Friday leaves its price close to where that rebound started.

The four-hour chart shows the difficulty even more clearly when observed. Throughout October, successive recoveries have generally stopped at lower prices. Buyers have managed to interrupt the decline, but they have not been able to build on those gains.

The daily chart also shows how much September’s strength has faded. XLM traded above $0.23 late that month before slipping below $0.18 in October.

What would make this bounce more convincing?

The first improvement would be if it returns above the $0.179–$0.181 price area, followed by XLM then being able to hold that level as it tries to change the trend into a positive one.

That would put the price above its nearest short-term averages, and it will show that buyers are gaining some control.

But the harder test lies around the $0.184–$0.187 price area, because that was where the latest rebound ran out of steam. Moving through that area would interrupt the pattern of recoveries ending at lower prices.

Even then, a wider turnaround would require more progress. The daily chart’s longer-term averages remain overhead, clustered around the $0.188–$0.192 price area.

The recent lows still matter

For now, the $0.174–$0.175 price range looks like the area that buyers need to defend. This is because XLM has visited this range repeatedly in recent sessions.

If the price settles below it and it’s not able to recover, the recent lows around the $0.171–$0.172 price area become an area to watch.

If the price falls briefly below the support area, it’s fine, but if it continues to trade below it, it means decline has set in. Until either buyers reclaim higher ground or those lows give way, it will not be able to complete its recovery from its October decline.

Final Summary

XLM’s modest bounce has recovered only a small portion of its latest decline.

Holding $0.174–$0.175 and recovering $0.181 would improve the immediate outlook.

data.title: Initia halts L1 and rollups after $2.7 million exploit — What happened?
data.description:
Initia, a Layer 1 blockchain and interwoven modular roll-up network, suffered a major security incident on 23rd October. An attacker allegedly exploited a vulnerability in its blockchain to create tokens without permission and withdraw real assets from cross-chain bridges. 

According to the investigation, the attack began at 14:59:26 UTC when the exploiter used a single signed transaction to mint 2 million AUSD tokens out of thin air on Initia.

The transaction reportedly consumed 135,888 gas and called a ‘Move’ function directly, without requiring a cross-chain bridge message. So, instead of breaking the bridge’s security verification process directly, the attacker hacked a vulnerability in the token-minting mechanism.

All about Initia’s security incident

The attacker didn’t stop there though. Instead, they exploited cross-chain infrastructure to convert these unauthorized tokens into real assets on Ethereum [ETH]. So, roughly 153 seconds after the initial mint, a valid LayerZero message enabled the release of 1.4 million AUSD from the Ethereum-side adapter.

At the same time, the attacker also withdrew 105 ETH from the native-ETH adapter and obtained 1.08 million USDC through Circle’s Cross-Chain Transfer Protocol (CCTP). According to researchers, the attacker converted the funds into Ethereum through decentralized trading services, including 1inch and 0x.

Here, within approximately 7 minutes of the initial mint, around $2.65 million had reached Ethereum. The consolidated funds later amounted to 1,135.52 ETH, worth approximately $2.73 million, held in a newly created wallet.

This seemed to be very similar to September’s Liquid Network incident, where a software bug enabled the creation of unauthorized L-BTC and the withdrawal of real Bitcoin.

As expected, the incident forced Initia to halt its L1 blockchain and roll-ups. And yet, despite this rollercoaster, Initia’s token INIT was trading at $0.1484 at press time after a hike of 11.7% in the last 24 hours. 

2026 has so far being a tricky year for security incidents like these. In fact, AMBCrypto’s recent report found that crypto security losses surged by 55% to $1.18 billion in Q3 2026, while reported incidents jumped from 67 to 107. 

Final Summary

  • Transaction reportedly consumed 135,888 gas and called a ‘Move’ function directly, without requiring a cross-chain bridge message.
  • This was very similar to September’s Liquid Network incident, where a software bug enabled the creation of unauthorized L-BTC and the withdrawal of real Bitcoin.

data.title: Ethereum’s deflationary edge fades – Is an ETH/BTC breakout still possible?
data.description:
Ethereum’s [ETH] deflationary edge over Bitcoin may be fading.

Since the merge, 55.4% of the newly issued ETH has been burned. However, this number has dropped significantly to only 2.7% over the last thirty days. In addition, ETH’s yearly supply growth has increased to 0.86%, which is almost Bitcoin’s 0.82%. That’s a sharp pullback in ETH burning, impacting its scarcity argument and potentially challenging the long-term bullish thesis versus BTC.

So, with ETH’s deflationary narrative being challenged, its next leg higher could increasingly rely on demand for Ethereum’s Layer 1 block space. As the chart below shows, gas prices have dropped from 2.76 Gwei to just 0.03 Gwei in two days, fueling the “Is ETH the new SOL?” debate. But cheaper prices are not always good, as they can also signal weaker demand for the block space.

Notably, this is where a key on-chain metric comes into play. 

According to CryptoQuant data, Ethereum Velocity is at 11.03, implying that ETH is circulated actively on the blockchain. Moreover, the number of active addresses has hit 627k, suggesting growing adoption. And if the demand is sustained on a declining gas fee, the cost to transact on ETH will remain cheap despite active use.

In this context, declining gas fees could be a bullish sign, which brings ETH/BTC back to the forefront. While Ethereum’s deflationary edge is being eroded, strong Layer 1 activity could offset it. The important question is whether ongoing on-chain demand will catalyze a rebound in ETH/BTC. In turn, translate into a stronger relative performance against Bitcoin [BTC].

Ethereum’s bullish positioning raises hopes of BTC outperformance

The divergence between ETH’s technical and fundamental setup is growing interesting.

While the overall whale activity seems to be cooling, the Bitfinex whales’ ETH long positions are rising sharply, suggesting smart money is positioning for further upside. Meanwhile, ETH/BTC is also showing a pattern similar to its pre-altseason setup in 2021, forming higher highs and retesting its trendline.

On-chain data adds another bullish sign. According to Santiment, about 169k ETH left exchanges on a net basis. This marked the largest daily outflow in more than four months. A similar development occurred on the 5th of June when roughly 223,800 ETH left exchanges as ETH reached its lowest price since the beginning of April 2025, only to climb rapidly in the following days.

Taken together, strong network activity, rising whale longs, and a significant ETH exchange outflow make up Ethereum’s bullish case. Should ETH/BTC follow the same pattern as it did in 2021 ahead of the altseason, another breakout could be on the way.

The logic is simple: While Ethereum’s advantage over Bitcoin in terms of deflationary properties has weakened, an increase in layer 1 demand, rising whale longs, and ongoing exchange outflows may create conditions for a supply squeeze. Taken together, these factors suggest ETH could be building momentum for a potential breakout against BTC once the market turns back to risk-on.

Final Summary

data.title: Here’s why XRP’s price recovery faces threat from surge in whale inflows
data.description:
The Spot ETF flows to XRP in October have totaled +$14.52 million so far. The ETF inflows were not enough to halt the 13.4% price decline in October though, with the altcoin falling from $1.49 to $1.29 at the time of writing.

In mid-September, XRP tested the $1.25 local demand zone and saw a bullish price reaction that boosted the token up to $1.65. The retracement since then, including the steady losses in October, has driven the price back to the same demand zone.

XRP bulls look to hold on to $1.25 for a second time

AMBCrypto recently reported that the share of exchange transactions amounting to more than one million XRP dropped from 60% to 38.6%. It highlighted a slowdown in large-holder transfers, and their lower accumulation interest could help explain XRP’s price decline.

While the swing structure on the 1-day chart remained bullish, XRP settled into a range formation in recent months. The $1.27-$1.31 demand zone is the one swing traders will want to watch, anticipating a bullish price reaction.

Increased whale inflows threaten recovery potential

Crypto intelligence platform Santiment observed that the number of non-empty wallets on the XRP Ledger has been rising steadily, despite the price volatility in recent months.

Moreover, the number of new XRP wallets created in a day jumped to 4,772, the fifth-biggest spike this metric has seen since March. Fresh participation and holder growth could boost demand too.

At the same time, XRP inflows from whales (defined as exceeding 1 million tokens) to Binance have accelerated in recent weeks. The monthly inflow average has increased from $72 million in August to $112.4 million. These figures are the highest since March, according to crypto analyst Darkfost.

In fact, they were above the $90 million monthly average recorded in the past three months, and there have been daily spikes of $400 million, reinforcing the claim that whale selling has intensified.

Right now, whale inflows have retraced to typical levels, but a trend in the opposite direction would be more encouraging for investors and swing traders looking to buy at the $1.25 demand zone.

Final Summary

  • On-chain activity with holder growth and new wallets created on the XRP Ledger reflected positively on the altcoin.
  • Steady selling pressure, including from whales, drove the drawdown from $1.65 to $1.29.

data.title: Starknet TVL crashes 3.7x to $42M after getting 93% vote to become L1
data.description:
Starknet got an overwhelming vote approval to become an independent layer 1 (L1) chain, but suffered a massive DeFi activity blow. The Ethereum L2 saw its total value locked (TVL) drop by 3.7x (73%) from $158M to $42M on 22nd October. 

The crash was triggered by Extended, a decentralized perpetual futures exchange, which migrated from Starknet to Circle-backed Arc blockchain. The platform had a strategic partnership with Circle and sought higher performance. 

Extended migrated $120M in TVL, suggesting that it was the sole driver of Starknet’s DeFi activity. 

Similarly, Starknet’s stablecoin liquidity dropped by 75% from $147M to $37M over the same period. The bridged volumes also crashed, underscoring the dominance the Extended had in the L2. 

Will Starknet hold up after 93% support for L1 migration?

That said, Starknet plans to transition from an Ethereum L2 to an independent L1. The Starknet team, led by Eli Ben-Sasson, first floated the idea in early October.

Ben-Sasson argued that Ethereum’s post-quantum plan is too slow and may undermine the chain’s security plans amid increasing double threats from advanced AI models and quantum breakthroughs. 

A formal proposal for the same was put to a governance vote on 15th October. The proposal got massive 93% support, urging Starknet to research ways to become an L1. 

Following the vote, Sasson said StarkWare and the Starknet Foundation will allocate resources to begin the research. He added, 

STRK will remain the token of the network. Any path to transition to an L1 will be brought to a community vote. This is a huge shift and a milestone, but the AI and quantum challenges ahead require it.

Despite the overwhelming vote approval, however, STRK’s price chart was surprisingly negative. 

Starknet’s STRK reverses October gains

In early October, the L1 proposal sent STRK rallying by over +120% from $0.05 to $0.12. However, what followed was intense profit-taking, triggering a 58% loss and effectively reversing October’s gains. 

In fact, the pullback slipped below the EMA (exponential moving average) band. Simply put, STRK flipped bearish and shed another 7% on 22nd October. Unless the broader market sentiment improves, STRK could stay below the EMA bands for a while. 

Final Summary

  • Starknet TVL has crashed by 73% after Extended perps platform migrated $120M to Arc.
  • Team plans to begin L1 research pathways, but STRK reversed all of October’s gains.

data.title: Bitcoin sees $771M in whale withdrawals – Why BTC could reclaim $84K
data.description:
Institutional activity around Bitcoin [BTC] escalated as Fidelity and BlackRock received significant BTC transfers into their ETF wallets, suggesting fresh interest among these key asset managers.

According to Onchain Lens on X, Fidelity’s FBTC ETF wallet reportedly received 282.63 BTC valued around $23.08 million from Binance. Additionally, BlackRock’s ETF wallets also received 384.77 BTC, valued at approximately $31.4 million.

Combined, these transactions reflected a continued institutional activity despite Bitcoin’s latest price weakness.

Here it is important to note that even though wallet transfers alone could not validate fresh purchases, the movements strengthened the attention toward institutional Bitcoin positioning.

Beyond the institutional activity, another noteworthy accumulation activity emerged among newly created wallets.

Since the 1st of October, Bitcoin’s large holders additionally heightened their activity, with 40 newly created wallets withdrawing 9,458 BTC from Wintermute. These withdrawals totaled roughly $771.5 million, which reflected considerable movements among wallets potentially connected to large market players.

This concentration of withdrawals across the newly created addresses reinforced the chance of a well-coordinated accumulation ahead of a possible price recovery. In fact, such transfers often attract attention since investors sometimes move acquired Bitcoin into wallets for longer-term custody.

The broader exchange activity meanwhile provided additional context for assessing whether BTC holders were indeed reducing their available exchange supply.

BTC exchange withdrawals deepen amid reserve decline

Bitcoin‘s Spot market registered around -$465.55 million in Spot Netflows on the 22nd of October, validating the withdrawal narrative. For context, this negative netflow implied that more BTC left exchanges than entered during the reporting period.

Interestingly, Bitcoin’s USD-denominated exchange reserves fell 1.35% over 24 hours, reaching roughly $226.33 billion. These figures together pointed towards reduced exchange balances, even though Bitcoin’s valuation also influenced the dollar-denominated reserve metric.

Importantly, the continued withdrawals could reduce the immediately available selling supply in case holders continued moving coins away from trading platforms.

Now with institutional accumulation and whale withdrawals dominating the recent activity, Bitcoin’s price structure became increasingly important.

Bitcoin demand zone strengthens as SAR flips

Bitcoin’s daily timeframe chart highlighted buyers defending an important order block around the $81k price region.

Following the most recent price rebound, BTC traded around $81,764 at press time, maintaining its position above the identified demand region. Importantly, the Parabolic SAR had just flipped below price, with its dots visibly at $80,001, suggesting improving bullish conditions amid the earlier decline.

Meanwhile, the Money Flow Index (MFI) indicator stood at 53.74, implying moderately positive buying pressure as capital inflows slightly outweighed outflows. Overall, institutional transfers, whale withdrawals, and declining exchange balances favored a  bullish outlook as BTC defended its key support level.

Bitcoin, therefore, stands a better chance of extending its recovery toward $84,000 so long as buyers continue defending the demand zone supported by the bullish Parabolic SAR reversal.

Final Summary

  • Institutional Bitcoin transfers and $771.5 million in whale withdrawals highlighted growing accumulation activity.
  • BTC held its demand zone as the bullish SAR flip strengthened recovery attempts toward $84,000.
